title: LANCET: An open-source programmable thermal-sequencing cartridge platform for sequential multi-step point-of-care biochemistry
description: Hardware design files, Arduino firmware, and validation protocols for the Lambert iGEM 2025 LANCET cartridge: an open-source programmable thermal-sequencing cartridge platform that drives arbitrary multi-step biochemistry inside a single closed 3D-printed polycarbonate tube. Tunable paraffin-mineral oil wax valves at programmable melt thresholds release reagents in turn under a software-defined thermal protocol delivered by an Arduino Uno + N-MOSFET + DS18B20 controller, at a durable hardware cost of $48.58 USD. The substrate is in principle chemistry-agnostic and supports CRISPR-Cas12a / Cas13, LAMP, sample-preparation cascades, and other multi-step point-of-care chemistries; the demonstrated instantiation reported in the companion HardwareX paper is a dual-threshold valve set (10:7 mass ratio melting at 45 C; 10:8 melting at 50 C) and a five-phase Arduino protocol that runs an RPA -> Cas12a -> reporter workflow for early-window Lyme diagnosis. Companion repository for the HardwareX paper.

Documentation (Markdown files, BOM CSV, validation protocols) is released under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE-HARDWARE, LICENSE-FIRMWARE, and LICENSE-DOCS in the repository root. The platform is in principle chemistry-agnostic; only the RPA-Cas12a Lyme application has been demonstrated in this release.
